sections.text: Modernizing legacy systems is enterprise IT's hardest problem — not because the code is exotic, but because every line carries decades of undocumented business rules. This is the Astra Harness — Nous's accelerator for legacy modernization.

Today, we walk MINPACK — fifty Fortran files, sixty subroutines — to dot-NET eight. We open H Y B R D one, and ask Claude to draft a behavioural specification. This isn't a generic prompt. Nous ships a calibrated prompt library, pinned per source language and target stack, that produces structured citable claims.

What comes back is not code. It is invariants, side effects, edge cases, open questions — every claim tied to specific source lines. The taxonomy comes from Nous's Fortran spec schema. We ship parallel schemas for COBOL, with R P G and P L slash one on our roadmap.

The expert — not the AI — signs off. The signature is cryptographic, bound to this exact source revision. If the Fortran changes by a byte, the signature is automatically invalidated. If it does not, the signature carries forward — so you never re-validate code that hasn't changed. Every state transition lands in an immutable audit log, queryable as a SOX, HIPAA, or P C I evidence feed.

From the signed specification, the harness generates target-stack code. Nous ships scaffold archetypes per target — dot-NET eight here, Java Spring also in our catalog — with dependency injection, claim-mapped tests, and hash-traceable provenance.

Before the scaffold ships, three independent gates run. Compile. Test pack — every signed claim has an auto-generated fixture, and they all pass. Equivalence — the original Fortran, and the new C-sharp, are driven with the same inputs; outputs must match. Commit is blocked until every badge is green.

The commit lands in your existing Git workflow, with the validation attestation attached. And what you've just watched for H Y B R D one, repeats for the other fifty-nine routines — five of them, here, at speed.

Six signed specs. Six attestations. What Nous ships is the calibrated assets that make this work on day one — schemas per legacy language, tuned prompts, scaffold archetypes, three independent validation gates, and a compliance-ready audit feed. Months become weeks. Audit-grade by default. That is the time Nous gives you back.
